pharm: Competitive muscarinic (M3-selective) receptor antagonist that relaxes bladder detrusor smooth muscle, reducing involuntary contractions in overactive bladder.

summary: Darifenacin is an extended-release oral antimuscarinic agent with selectivity for the M3 receptor, used to treat overactive bladder with symptoms of urge urinary incontinence, urgency, and frequency. The usual starting dose is 7.5 mg once daily, increasing to 15 mg once daily based on response. It is contraindicated in urinary retention, gastric retention, and uncontrolled narrow-angle glaucoma. Because it is metabolized by CYP3A4, the dose should not exceed 7.5 mg/day with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors or in moderate hepatic impairment, and it carries the typical anticholinergic adverse effects of dry mouth and constipation.
indications: Treatment of overactive bladder with symptoms of urge urinary incontinence, urgency, and frequency

moa: Darifenacin is a competitive muscarinic receptor antagonist with greater affinity for the M3 receptor than for other muscarinic subtypes. M3 receptors mediate contraction of urinary bladder detrusor smooth muscle. By blocking M3 receptors, darifenacin reduces involuntary detrusor contractions, increases bladder capacity, and relieves the urgency, frequency, and urge incontinence of overactive bladder.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to darifenacin or its components (including reported angioedema)
relative: Clinically significant bladder outflow obstruction (risk of urinary retention)
Gastrointestinal obstructive disorders, severe constipation, ulcerative colitis (decreased GI motility)
Controlled narrow-angle glaucoma (use only if benefits outweigh risks)

preg: There are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women. Darifenacin should be used during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: It is not known whether darifenacin is excreted in human milk. Because many drugs are excreted in human milk, caution should be exercised when darifenacin is administered to a nursing woman.
renal: No dose adjustment is needed for patients with renal impairment. Darifenacin has been studied in renal impairment without clinically significant change requiring adjustment.
hepatic: In moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh B), the daily dose should not exceed 7.5 mg. Darifenacin is not recommended in severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C). No adjustment is needed in mild impairment.

major: Potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, itraconazole, ritonavir, nelfinavir, clarithromycin, nefazodone) - increase darifenacin; limit dose to 7.5 mg/day
Other anticholinergic agents - additive antimuscarinic toxicity
moderate: Drugs metabolized by CYP2D6 with narrow therapeutic index (e.g., flecainide, thioridazine, tricyclic antidepressants) - darifenacin inhibits CYP2D6; monitor
minor: Moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors - modest increase in exposure
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food.
interactions.alcohol: Alcohol may potentiate somnolence and CNS effects; use with caution.
interactions.diagnostics: No specific laboratory test interference reported.

counsel: Swallow the tablet whole with water - do not chew, crush, or divide it
Dry mouth and constipation are common; sip water, chew sugarless gum, and increase fiber/fluids
Do not drive or operate machinery until you know how this medicine affects you (it may cause drowsiness)
Tell your doctor if you have trouble urinating, severe constipation, eye pain, or swelling of the face, lips, or tongue
Tell your doctor about all other medicines, especially antifungals, HIV medicines, and clarithromycin
pk: Detrusor effects develop over days; steady state in about 6 days
Once-daily dosing maintains effect over 24 hours
Store at 25 C (77 F); excursions permitted 15-30 C (59-86 F)
pearls: M3-selective antimuscarinic - chosen for overactive bladder; M3 mediates bladder contraction
Contraindicated in urinary retention, gastric retention, and uncontrolled narrow-angle glaucoma
Cap dose at 7.5 mg/day with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors and in moderate hepatic impairment; avoid in severe hepatic impairment
Extended-release tablet must be swallowed whole
Anticholinergic burden adds to other antimuscarinics, antihistamines, and TCAs - watch elderly for confusion
missed: If a dose is missed, skip the missed dose and take the next dose at the regular time. Do not take two doses on the same day to make up for a missed dose.
overdose: Overdose with darifenacin can produce severe antimuscarinic effects (such as dry mouth, blurred/abnormal vision, urinary retention, and tachycardia). Treatment should be symptomatic and supportive, and ECG monitoring is recommended. In clinical trials doses up to 75 mg (five times the maximum therapeutic dose) produced effects limited to abnormal vision.
